[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Reshaping, Pivoting, and Melting in Pandas"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Data reshaping is a fundamental skill in data science. It allows you to transform your data frames into the exact structure required for analysis or machine learning modeling. In this tutorial, we will explore how to use Pandas to reshape data using stack, unstack, pivot, and melt operations."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Stacking and Unstacking DataFrames"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"The stack() method pivots the columns of the data frame into rows, while unstack() does the reverse, pivoting rows into columns. This is particularly useful when working with multi-index data frames."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"import pandas as pd

# Create sample multi-index data
data = {
    'City': ['New York', 'New York', 'London', 'London'],
    'Year': [2022, 2023, 2022, 2023],
    'Population': [8.3, 8.4, 8.9, 9.0]
}
df = pd.DataFrame(data).set_index(['City', 'Year'])
print("Original MultiIndex DataFrame:")
print(df)

# Unstack the inner index (Year) to columns
unstacked_df = df.unstack()
print("\nUnstacked DataFrame:")
print(unstacked_df)

# Stack it back
stacked_df = unstacked_df.stack()
print("\nStacked DataFrame:")
print(stacked_df)"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Pivoting DataFrames"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"The pivot() function is used to reshape data based on column values. It takes three primary arguments: index (columns to use to make new frame's index), columns (columns to use to make new frame's columns), and values (columns to use to populate new frame's values)."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"# Create sample data for pivoting
sales_data = {
    'Date': ['2023-01-01', '2023-01-01', '2023-01-02', '2023-01-02'],
    'Store': ['Store A', 'Store B', 'Store A', 'Store B'],
    'Sales': [200, 150, 220, 180]
}
df_sales = pd.DataFrame(sales_data)
print("Original Sales DataFrame:")
print(df_sales)

# Pivot the table
pivoted_df = df_sales.pivot(index='Date', columns='Store', values='Sales')
print("\nPivoted DataFrame:")
print(pivoted_df)"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Melting DataFrames (Wide to Long)"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"The melt() function does the exact opposite of pivoting. It transforms a wide format data frame into a long format. This is extremely useful for cleaning data where multiple columns represent values of the same variable."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"# Create wide format data
wide_data = {
    'Student': ['Alice', 'Bob'],
    'Math': [85, 90],
    'Science': [92, 88]
}
df_wide = pd.DataFrame(wide_data)
print("Wide Format DataFrame:")
print(df_wide)

# Melt the DataFrame
melted_df = pd.melt(df_wide, id_vars=['Student'], value_vars=['Math', 'Science'], 
                    var_name='Subject', value_name='Score')
print("\nMelted (Long Format) DataFrame:")
print(melted_df)"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Summary of Reshaping Operations"},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"stack() and unstack(): Best for moving between hierarchical index columns and rows."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"pivot(): Best for transforming long-form data into wide-form summary tables."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"melt(): Best for unpivoting wide-form data into long-form for analysis and plotting."}]
